what_landed: COUPLED_SCENARIOS gains the three secondary-delivery shapes: a packet the holder aimed at one subject and the engine lands on another. The pair snapshot's item sweep is single-target, so a cone, a cleave splash and a chained strike all price exactly zero there, and a roster is the only place any of them is observable. Step 2 of the fight-navigability plan moves that whole band into src/calculator/fight/items/secondary_delivery.py, so the band had no oracle at all until these three scenarios existed.

landed_against.rule: R-17: no committed leaf moves inside this commit; the coupled baseline gains three scenarios and moves none of the twenty-three it holds

arming_measurement.why: A covering scenario is evidence only if the mechanic it covers is armed in it. Each row below is worth zero against a single target, which is why two enemies and full auto uptime are on all three requests.
arming_measurement.reading: Three distinct deliveries. Titanic's cone declares its own max-health magnitude and strikes one packet per authored swing. Ravenous splashes a share of the swing and carries a copied on-hit stream beside it, so it is the one scenario holding both rows. Statikk's chain allocates one packet across a level-scaled prefix of the roster, and Blade of the Ruined King rides beside it because a chain with no on-hit sibling to copy observes only the packet's own magnitude. The Hydras are one exclusivity group, so they cannot share a roster.

what_did_not_move.claim: No number the engine computes moved. The three scenarios price the same on the pre-step-2 engine as on the refactored one.
evidence: scripts/golden_baseline.json: `python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json` reports 'snapshot identical'.

A `git archive HEAD` copy of the tree, with only scripts/golden_snapshot.py overlaid so the three scenarios exist there, produces `golden_snapshot.coupled_entry` output for all three that is byte-identical to the refactored tree's: sha256 a82c104644e7b043574be5b49bfafae12d14c3b49cb82ae099239ab29f6d40d4 on both sides.

scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json: the standing difference set is exactly the seven paths declared above, three absent scenarios plus four shape counters (leaves 96070 -> 124224, numeric_leaves 31671 -> 40444, entries and scenario_count 23 -> 26). Every leaf of the twenty-three committed scenarios is unchanged.

why_the_baselines_are_declared_and_not_c: golden_snapshot.require_committed_src refuses a capture while src/ differs from HEAD, because snapshot_provenance stamps `git rev-parse HEAD:src` and a capture over a dirty tree names a tree it did not read. So the scenarios and this receipt land first and the capture is the integration commit that follows, which is the same order R-17 and Amendment L, Ruling 2 already require: adding a covering scenario is its own act. Until that capture, `compare scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json` reports the seven paths above and tests/test_coupled_golden_allowlist.py is what reads them as claimed rather than as drift.
